quote: die Convergenz der Reihe für den singu- lären Punkt, bedarf einer besondern Unter- suchung.
english: the convergence of the series at the singular point requires a special investigation.
topic: The page concludes a remark on convergence of a power series on the boundary circle, then begins treating a curve f(x,y)=0 through the origin at an ordinary point, expanding x as a power series in y and dividing f(φ(y)+r, y) by r to obtain F(x,y).

triage.modern_statement: Let f(z)=Σ a_n z^n have radius of convergence R. Suppose f has a singular point z₀ on the boundary circle |z|=R, meaning it cannot be continued analytically there. Does the series Σ a_n z₀^n converge? This is the general question of how a power series behaves at singular points of its circle of convergence. The surrounding text on the page (convergence on the boundary circle, then series expansions at ordinary points of an algebraic curve) fits this reading. The fragment does not identify the specific series Hilbert had in mind, so this statement is for a general series.
triage.answered_by: This was not answered as one specific question. It is a standard classical topic, and the known answer is that no general rule exists: at a singular point the series may converge or diverge, so each case has to be checked separately. That is the 'special investigation' Hilbert mentions. The related theorem for regular boundary points is due to Fatou (1906) and M. Riesz (1916): if a_n → 0, the series converges at every regular point of the boundary, uniformly on closed arcs of regular points. Singular points are exactly the case this theorem leaves out. Erdős and others later studied refinements, such as over-convergence on the circle of convergence (Erdős's 1947 paper). The remark is not one of Hilbert's 23 problems or the 24th problem.

evidence.claim: M. Riesz proved that if a_n → 0 and f is regular at every point of an arc of the unit circle, then Σ a_n z^n converges to f uniformly on that arc. If a_n does not tend to 0, the series cannot converge at any point of the unit circle.
On the boundary of the disk of convergence, a power series can behave in complicated ways: it may converge at some points and diverge at others.

Standard theorems on convergence on the circle (e.g. for monotonically decreasing coefficients) give convergence at every point of |z|=1 with the possible exception of the singular point z=1, which has to be examined separately.
Recent work still generalizes the classical Fatou–Riesz theorem.

triage.why: Hilbert's remark is a standard caveat: knowing where the singularities are says nothing in general about convergence at a singular boundary point. Simple examples show both outcomes, e.g. Σ z^n/n² converges at its singular point z=1, while Σ z^n/n diverges there. The classical Fatou–Riesz theory deals with regular boundary points and deliberately leaves singular points to case-by-case analysis. That matches 'bedarf einer besondern Untersuchung' (requires a special investigation). Boundary behaviour of power series is still studied, as the 2023 arXiv generalization shows, but the basic question here is settled textbook material. Confidence is medium because the fragment is short and the exact series Hilbert meant (possibly the expansion φ(y) for the curve) is not identified.
